title: My Top 20 Favorite Foreign/Non English-Language Directors

commenti.body:
Fun! I’m going to throw out a few qualifiers to go along with my list. I won’t be including work by any Hollywood immigrants since that is in the spirit of the list and makes it more fun anyway, but I will shout them here: Lang, Lubitsch, Ludwig, Ophuls, Preminger, Renoir, Sirk, von Sternberg, von Stroheim, Tourneur, Ulmer, and Verhoeven. 

Then I’m going to do a separate list exclusively made up of filmmakers from France, Japan, and Italy because these countries make up a large majority of my favorites (and I’m still leaving out greats like Bava, Kurosawa, Leone, Resnais, Tati, and Zurlini). Unranked, alphabetical order: 

Michelangelo Antonioni - Italy

Dario Argento - Italy 

Robert Bresson - France 

Jean-Claude Brisseau - France 

Vittorio Cottafavi - Italy 

Marguerite Duras - France 

Jean-Luc Godard - France

Sacha Guitry - France 

Kiyoshi Kurosawa - Japan 

Kenji Mizoguchi - Japan 

Mikio Naruse - Japan 

Yasujiro Ozu - Japan 

Maurice Pialat - France 

Jacques Rivette - France 

Eric Rohmer - France 

Roberto Rossellini - Italy 

Jean-Claude Rousseau - France 

Hiroshi Shimizu - Japan 

Straub & Huillet - France

Luchino Visconti - Italy 

And finally, the more interesting list! This was really difficult to narrow down and I attempted to diversify as best I could, while still being true to what I love. Unranked, alphabetical order: 

Chantal Akerman - Belgium 

Ingmar Bergman - Sweden 

Julio Bressane- Brazil 

Luis Bunuel - Spain/Mexico 

Lav Diaz - Philippines 

Carl T. Dreyer - Denmark 

Sergei Eisenstein - Soviet 

Rainer Werner Fassbinder - Germany 

Miklos Jancso - Hungary 

Abbas Kiarostami - Iran 

Jose Cesar Monteiro - Portugal 

F.W. Murnau - Germany 

Manoel de Oliveira - Portugal 

Glauber Rocha - Brazil 

Raul Ruiz - Chile 

Jerzy Skolimowski - Poland 

Michael Snow - Canada

Andrei Tarkovsky - Soviet 

Wang Bing - China 

Edward Yang - Taiwan

Those are some great lists (Vinterberg is a solid pick for example). You've inspired me to check out each of those directors.

Here's just a few which immediately come to mind:

* Bong Joon-ho (South Korea)
* Fabian Bielinsky (Argentina)
* Hayao Miyazaki (Japan)
* Kim Ki-duk (South Korea)
* Lee Chang-dong (South Korea)
* Makoto Shinkai (Japan)
* Oriol Paulo (Spain)
* Sion Sono (Japan)

I am far too ignorant to make a list that does justice to what is out there, but from your list, Kieslowski, Yang, Kore-eda and Kiarostami would probably be on my list too. Zhang Yimou and Von Trier would make my list. On the strength of the single film I have seen by each of them, I would be tempted to include the directors of "Happy as Lazzaro", "Babette's Feast", "The Metamorphosis of Birds", "Lola Rennt" and "Jesus of Montreal". But undoubtedly my favourite would be Tarkovsky (I have seen all his features except Nostalghia) and I might include other Soviet or former Soviet directors.

I'm going to embarrass myself, and list the directors whose works I've most enjoyed, even if some of the works are quite lightweight. I've also included immigrants if they've a body of work prior.

Grouped by countries

Jackie Chan - Hong Kong

John Woo - Hong Kong

Pedro Almodóvar - Spain

Julio Medem - Spain

Dario Argento - Italy

Patrice Leconte - France

Luc Besson - France

François Ozon - France

Bertrand Tavernier - France

Guillermo del Toro - Mexico

Andrei Tarkovsky - Russia

Aleksandr Sokurov - Russia

Timur Bekmambetov - Russia\\Kazakhstan

Ishirô Honda - Japan

Hayao Miyazaki - Japan

Akira Kurosawa - Japan

Shinya Tsukamoto - Japan

Mamoru Oshii - Japan

This is an interesting exercise. I'll probably revise it as more directors spring to mind. I also feel bad I haven't included a more diverse selection, as I love cinema from inchoate film industries.

I'm realizing I watch more English-language films than I thought! Difficult to leave out the Americans, Canadians, and Brits. If I've only seen one film by a director, I didn't include them here even though I loved that one film I did see (e.g. Satyajit Ray, Asghar Farhadi). The other lists on this thread are great reminders (e.g. I should finally watch something by Kore-eda and more Ray).
